submitted.rationale: Index 4 (Nb 0.456, V 0.544) had the highest photocurrent measured, 8.56e-6 A. Photocurrent rose as V increased: -3.17e-6 A at Nb 0.714, 6.26e-6 A at Nb 0.505 and 8.56e-6 A at Nb 0.456. This agrees with MEGNet, which predicts that the V-rich Nb-V-O phases (NbV2O7 2.36 eV, NbVO4 1.47 eV) absorb the 3.22 eV illumination.

rejected.reason: Negative photocurrent (-3.17e-6 A) at the Nb-rich end.

consultations.verdict: Support: Nb9V2O25 (Nb-rich, ~0.82 Nb) predicted HSE gap 2.70 eV, below 3.22 eV photon energy, so it absorbs; NbVO5 (0.5 Nb) is near-hull but gap 3.48 eV > photon energy. Nb-richest candidate 13 is closest to the absorbing Nb9V2O25 phase field.
Support: V-rich phases NbV2O7 (gap 2.36 eV) and NbVO4 (1.47 eV) absorb at 3.22 eV. The Nb-rich end (idx 13) gave a negative photocurrent, so I'm moving to the V-richest candidate, index 4.

Weak support: NbVO4 (Nb 0.5) is near-hull (0.026 eV/atom) and absorbing (1.47 eV). Index 11 (Nb 0.505) sits at that 1:1 stoichiometry, and the GP gives it the highest mean among the unmeasured points. The trend so far favors the V-rich/1:1 region.
